questions.prompt: In ideal projectile motion (no air resistance), the horizontal acceleration is:
options: Equal to the initial horizontal velocity
questions.explanation: Gravity acts only vertically. The horizontal component of velocity is constant throughout the flight; the horizontal acceleration is zero. The vertical acceleration is g downward.

questions.prompt: A projectile is launched with initial speed u = 20 m/s at 30° to the horizontal (g = 10 m/s²). What is its time of flight T?
For a projectile launched from ground level with fixed initial speed, what launch angle gives the maximum horizontal range?
questions.explanation: Range R = u² sin(2θ) / g. sin(2θ) peaks when 2θ = 90°, i.e. θ = 45°. (Air resistance shifts this slightly, but in the ideal case 45° wins.)
